[[File:Shimonomiya Chikatsu Jinja Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
**Chikatsu Shrine** (近津神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Daigo, Ibaraki|en|Daigo, Ibaraki|qid=Q1346817|lt=Daigo, Ibaraki}}, {{ill|Kuji District, Ibaraki|ceb|Kuji-gun|es|Distrito de Kuji (Ibaraki)|fr|District de Kuji|id|Distrik Kuji, Ibaraki|it|Distretto di Kuji|ja|久慈郡|ko|구지군|pl|Powiat Kuji|th|อำเภอคูจิ|uk|Повіт Кудзі|vi|Kuji, Ibaraki|zh|久慈郡|qid=Q1075212|lt=Kuji District}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|en|Ibaraki Prefecture|qid=Q83273|lt=Ibaraki Prefecture}}, Japan. It is considered a debated shrine under the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} system and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|Gōsha}}. It is also commonly referred to as **Shimonomiya Chikatsu Shrine**.
== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it was established by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}, with the shrine buildings constructed in the 4th year of the {{ill|Keiun|en|Keiun|qid=Q428753|lt=Keiun era}} (707). During the {{ill|Kōhei|fa|کوهی (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōhei|ia|Kohei|id|Kōhei|ja|康平|ko|고헤이 (연호)|ru|Кохэй|simple|Kōhei|sr|Кохеи|tr|Kōhei|zh|康平 (日本)|zh_yue|康平|qid=Q1193572|lt=Kōhei era}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} donated 3,000 kanmon to the shrine.
== Shrine Grounds ==
* **Hoko-sugi (鉾スギ)** – A designated {{ill|Natural Monument of Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|Natural Monument of Ibaraki Prefecture}}. This sacred tree is 43 meters tall with a trunk circumference of 9.6 meters and is estimated to be over 1,200 years old. It is believed to have been planted when the shrine was first established.

== Festivals and Rituals ==
; **Nakataue of Chikatsu Shrine**
: A rice planting festival held annually on the {{ill|Summer solstice|en|Summer solstice|qid=Q7603898|lt=summer solstice}}. It is said to have originated with rice offerings donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|en|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|qid=Q1194944|lt=Tokugawa Mitsukuni}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, suggesting the ritual dates back to the mid-Edo period. Sacred ropes ({{ill|Shimenawa|en|Shimenawa|qid=Q1887421|lt=shimenawa}}) are set around the rice fields, and after purification rites by the head priest, a group of young women (saotome) plant rice seedlings to the accompaniment of drums, flutes, and songs.
; **Omase Mawashi (御桝廻し)**
: An ancient ritual once practiced at the "Three Chikatsu Shrines" ({{ill|Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine|ja|Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine}}, {{ill|Yatsugi Tsutsukowake Shrine|ja|Yatsugi Tsutsukowake Shrine}}, and Shimonomiya Chikatsu Shrine) and later adopted by neighboring shrines. On October 28, a ritual rice measure (masu) filled with newly harvested rice is wrapped in straw matting and adorned with sacred wands (heisoku), then enshrined in a special hut. After seven years, it is passed to the next designated shrine with fresh rice.
These rituals reflect the shrine’s role as a guardian deity of agriculture, with similar practices found throughout {{ill|Daigo, Ibaraki|en|Daigo, Ibaraki|qid=Q1346817|lt=Daigo, Ibaraki}} and {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|qid=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture}}, indicating a wide agricultural belief system spanning northern {{ill|Hitachi Province|en|Hitachi Province|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi Province}} and southern {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province}}.
== Access ==
* A 5-minute walk from {{ill|Shimonomiya Station|en|Shimonomiya Station|qid=Q7497007|lt=Shimonomiya Station}} on the {{ill|Suigun Line|de|Suigun-Linie|es|Línea Suigun|fr|Ligne Suigun|it|Linea Suigun|ja|水郡線|ko|스이군선|tl|Linyang Suigun|zh|水郡線|qid=Q1056202|lt=Suigun Line}}, operated by {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}}.
